summary: The README explains the four blocks, the tracker and the verification layers clearly, but it overstates the guardrail hooks: Cursor's docs say beforeMCPExecution doesn't run in cloud agents, and a localhost exception would let a client reach production through the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy. The quick start leaves out prerequisites the SOP and Cursor require, the Block 1 summary tells people to apply IaC at the wrong time, and the eval and source claims go further than the hill-climb log and sources.json support.

findings.claim: The README cites S-47 as documenting beforeMCPExecution as supported and uses hooks as the backstop for database MCP tools. Cursor's hooks page lists beforeMCPExecution under 'Hooks not available in cloud agents', and Projects run on Cloud Agents. The documented cloud-agent hook sources also don't include plugin hooks, and hooks don't run during early read-only turns.
findings.evidence: README line 144: "Cursor documents `beforeShellExecution` and `beforeMCPExecution` as supported ([S-47])". README line 77: "Hooks deny ... database MCP tools". https://cursor.com/docs/hooks, fetched 2026-11-04, under 'Hooks not available in cloud agents': "beforeMCPExecution / afterMCPExecution Deferred while cloud agents can still start in a read-only environment, where hooks don't load and MCP hook timing is unclear." Also: "Cloud agents load hooks from these sources: Project hooks (.cursor/hooks.json in your repo) ... Team hooks (Enterprise) ... Enterprise hooks (Enterprise)" and "Hooks do not run during those turns." S-47's quote list covers only beforeShellExecution.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the S-47 claim, and for MCP guarding in cloud agents use preToolUse with tool_name MCP:<tool_name>. Either ship the hooks as .cursor/hooks.json in the Project's workspace repo or as Enterprise team hooks, or say plainly that the MCP and plugin-hook backstop is absent in Projects until the pilot proves otherwise.

findings.claim: The hook allows database clients that name an explicit local host. The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy, the usual way to reach Cloud SQL, listens on localhost by default, so the hook would let a psql command reach production or a clone through a running proxy. The README presents the hook as a backstop for 'never connect to production' and doesn't mention this case.
findings.evidence: README line 77: "Hooks deny database clients without an explicit local host". README line 73: "Agents never connect to production, a clone or a replica." https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-proxy/main/README.md: "starts the Proxy listening on localhost with the default database engine port ... Postgres localhost:5432".
findings.suggested_fix: State that the localhost exception doesn't separate a local Docker test database from a proxied production instance. Either tighten the hook (for example, allow only the test harness's container or socket), or list 'no Auth Proxy running in agent environments' as a requirement and a pilot check.

findings.claim: The Block 1 summary tells people to 'apply the IaC after the upgrade'. The SOP has the DBA apply the flag IaC (removing blocking flags) during Block 1, and that change is needed to pass G1.1. Only the database_version change waits until after the upgrade. A team lead following the README could hold back the flag fix, and Cloud SQL would then block the upgrade.
findings.evidence: README line 38: "People: review and merge every PR, and apply the IaC after the upgrade." SOP line 129, B1-03: "Flags: remove blocking and removed flags ... Agent drafts the IaC PR, DBA applies". SOP line 81: "Cloud SQL blocks the MVU on `vacuum_defer_cleanup_age` and `force_parallel_mode` [S-01]". SOP line 137, B1-11: only the version change "merges after the runbook's upgrade step, as a reconcile".
findings.suggested_fix: Say that people apply flag and other source-compatible IaC in Block 1, and that only the database_version change is planned now and applied as a reconcile after the upgrade.

findings.claim: The quick start leaves out prerequisites that the SOP and Cursor require before the bootstrap can work. These are the customer's written statement of what agents may touch, a DBA who has agreed to run the queries, source-control access to every org the bootstrap searches, the tracker-backend and Slack connections, a Teams or Enterprise plan for a team marketplace, and Cursor 3.21.9 or later for Enterprise teams.
findings.evidence: README lines 81-85 list only install, create Project, paste the prompt, approve, and send the precheck. SOP lines 29-31, Block 0 entry: "The customer has said in writing what agents may and may not touch. A DBA has agreed to run read-only queries". https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent: "Before anyone can start a cloud agent from a repository, a Cursor account admin needs to connect source control". S-45: "Team marketplaces are available on Teams and Enterprise plans". S-40: "Enterprise teams need Cursor 3.21.9 or later" (confirmed live on https://cursor.com/docs/agent/projects).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step 0 'Before you start' listing the written agent-scope agreement, the DBA commitment, source-control access to every org, the tracker MCP and Slack connections, and the plan and version requirements, with their sources.

findings.claim: The README presents skill evals as one of the four layers that verify the work, but it doesn't report the results. The latest measured round in the hill-climb log still fails 3 of 16 hard-gate cases on Opus and 4 of 16 on composer. One of those failures is an agent trying `gh pr merge`, which only the hook stopped. Round 2's levers have no recorded results.
findings.evidence: README line 65: "Hard gates check decisions and output shape, and a judge ... scores against an answer key." README line 74: "Agents open PRs, and never merge". evals/HILLCLIMB.md line 62: "Hard-gate passes | 13/16 | 12/16". Line 70: "`guardrails/merge-request`, composer: it tried `gh pr merge`. The hook blocked it". The Round 2 section (lines 74-84) has no results link or table.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the current pass rates per model in the README and list the cases still failing, including the merge attempt. Mark Round 2 as unmeasured until its results are recorded.

findings.claim: The README says it's written for Cloud SQL and that the precheck SQL is tested. The evidence in the bundle shows the kit only ran on community Postgres in Docker, with Cloud SQL-only rows patched in by hand. The pilot checklist, which says it lists what couldn't be tested, doesn't include running the kit on a real Cloud SQL instance. On Cloud SQL nobody is superuser, and views like pg_stats silently show fewer rows, so a partial result could look clean.
findings.evidence: README line 67: "The precheck SQL itself is tested on Postgres 14 and 18, as superuser and as a read-only role". evals/HILLCLIMB.md line 84: "runs the real kit with psql on Postgres 14 in Docker. It then patches in what a container can't produce: ... a `cloudsqladmin` row". SOP line 80: "community PostgreSQL 14 to 18 (not Cloud SQL)". S-05: "customers cannot create or have access to users with superuser attributes".
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Run the precheck kit as cloudsqlsuperuser on a real Cloud SQL 14 instance and check every section returns rows' to the pilot checklist, and say in the README that the kit hasn't yet run on Cloud SQL.

findings.claim: Many files the README and bootstrap prompt depend on aren't in the reviewed bundle, so I couldn't confirm they exist or match their descriptions. They include tracker-check.mjs, render-dashboard.mjs, the dashboard snapshot, automations.md, sources.md, catch-up-handoff-template.md, docs/reviews/*, evals/results/ and tests/sql/run-precheck.sh. The 'Already under way?' path and the daily status setup can't be followed without them.
findings.evidence: README links on lines 53-55, 63-65, 67 and 87 point to plugins/pg-major-upgrade/scripts/*.mjs, reference/automations.md, reference/sources.md, reference/catch-up-handoff-template.md, docs/reviews/2026-11-template-review-round-*.md, evals/results/ and tests/. The bundle contains only README.md, docs/bootstrap-prompt.md, evals/HILLCLIMB.md, reference/sources.json, and plugins/pg-major-upgrade/reference/{sop.md,tracker-schema.md}. The anchor sop.md#8-adapting-to-another-provider does resolve.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm that every linked file exists in the shipped repo, and make tests/check-template.mjs fail on any broken relative link in README.md and docs/.

findings.claim: The README says all 48 sources come with the exact quotes they were checked against, and that every claim cites a public source. In sources.json, S-34 to S-37 have no lastChecked, status or verified fields, and S-10 has status 'changed'. The SOP also includes an Inferred claim based on the authors' own unpublished test.
findings.evidence: README line 63: "lists 48 sources ... each with the exact quotes it was checked against" and "Every claim cites a public source." reference/sources.json lines 620-657: S-34, S-35, S-36 and S-37 have only id, title, url, supports and quotes. Line 156: S-10 "status": "changed". SOP line 80: "That's an internal observation with no public source, so treat it as Inferred." I fetched the S-10 page, and its quotes are still present.
findings.suggested_fix: Run check-sources on S-34 to S-37 and settle S-10's 'changed' status, or say in the README how many sources are currently verified. Reword the claim to 'every claim cites a public source or carries an Inferred or Unverified label'.

findings.claim: The stage summaries leave out or simplify gate conditions a team lead would need to explain. Block 1's exit leaves out the SCRAM password resets (G1.4), monitoring (G1.5) and the planned-not-applied IaC (G1.7). Block 2 makes 'sentinels arrive exactly once' mandatory, but the SOP also accepts a timed full re-snapshot. Block 3 places both go or no-go calls on the night, but the first one is at T-1 day.
findings.evidence: README line 39: "blockers are fixed in production, tests pass on the target version, connectors support it, and the runbook is reviewed (G1.1 to G1.7)." SOP lines 117-121 (G1.4, G1.5, G1.7). SOP line 169, G2.5: "Or a full re-snapshot of every affected consumer, plus downstream catch-up, was timed and fits." SOP line 282: "T-1 day ... Go or no-go 1".
findings.suggested_fix: List each gate's condition in a short phrase, or link each block summary to its gate table in the SOP.

findings.claim: The README never names the roles that approve gates. In particular it doesn't mention the business approver, who owns the data-loss rule and must sign the fix-forward decision. It also never says that rolling back after writes reopen loses every write made since. A team lead couldn't say who approves what, or what 'point of no return' costs.
findings.evidence: README line 47: "The first write on the new version is the point of no return." README line 29: "a named person approves it". SOP line 23: "The business approver owns the window and the data-loss rule." SOP line 301: "After reopening: a restore would drop every write since ... Plan to fix forward, and have the business approver sign that in the decision record."
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short roles list, and one sentence under Block 3 saying that after reopening the plan is to fix forward, with the business approver's signature.

findings.claim: For a migration already under way, the README says to paste the bootstrap prompt and then run /pg-catch-up. Once approved, the bootstrap's step 5 starts readiness scans and drafts a new precheck request before catch-up has loaded the existing results. It also turns every unknown into a question row that the handoff may already answer. The README doesn't say whether to approve step 5 before running catch-up.
findings.evidence: README line 87: "paste the bootstrap prompt, then run `/pg-catch-up`." docs/bootstrap-prompt.md line 30: "5. After I approve: start one read-only readiness scan per approved repo, draft the precheck request for the DBA". Line 37: "Paste the bootstrap prompt with the values you know, and run `/pg-catch-up`".
findings.suggested_fix: Say explicitly to stop at the bootstrap's approval step, run /pg-catch-up, and only then approve step 5. Alternatively, give a catch-up variant of the prompt that skips step 5.

findings.claim: Round 1 was kept even though composer's hard-gate passes dropped from 13 to 12 and a case that passed at baseline failed. That breaks the log's own rule to keep a change only if nothing regresses on any model. Round 2's levers also don't list the cases that lock them in. As a result, the README's eval layer reads as more rigorous than it was.
findings.evidence: evals/HILLCLIMB.md line 3: "keep the change only if the target improves and nothing regresses on any model. Each kept change is locked with a case that would have failed before it." Line 62: "12/16" against the baseline "13/16" at line 30. Line 71: "`tracker/backend-down`, composer: ... It passed at baseline, so this looks like run-to-run variance." Line 72: "keep the round 1 changes".
findings.suggested_fix: Rerun backend-down several times to show it's variance before calling it that, or amend the stated rule. Name the locking case for each Round 2 lever.

findings.claim: The hill-climb log says the template's tooling ran against a private customer tracker seed. The README describes the fixtures as synthetic and the content as public-only. A reader can't tell whether customer material was used in building or testing the template.
findings.evidence: evals/HILLCLIMB.md line 82: "It immediately caught a free-text Evidence value in a private customer tracker seed, which is now fixed." README line 128: "public-only content". README line 151: "The evals use synthetic fixtures".
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the reference or reword it to make clear no customer data entered the template or eval runs. Confirm that check-template's public-only scan covers evals/.
